Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

comment noun

a remark

also remark, make a comment, a passing remark

classical

Cic. Fam. 7.32.1: omnia omnium dicta … in mē cōnferrī
Traupman 353: dictum incūriōsum, offhand remark

dictum, dictī n.

noun, second declension

a remark, something said

Lewis & Short: “something said, i. e. a saying, a word”; often a witty one, as in Cicero’s letter. To comment on something is to say something about it: dē eā rē dīcere (see say).

Examples

  • ais enim, ut ego discesserim, omnia omnium dicta … in mē cōnferrī

    for you say that since I left, every witty remark anyone makes is being put down to meCic. Fam. 7.32.1

See also comment, say, statement.
